# dgesvx

> Computes the solution to system of linear equations A·X = B for general matrices.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import dgesvx from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/dgesvx';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
dgesvx(
    order,
    fact, trans,
    N, nrhs,
    A, LDA,
    AF, LDAF,
    IPIV, strideIPIV,
    equed,
    r, strideR,
    c, strideC,
    B, LDB,
    X, LDX,
    rcond,
    FERR, strideFERR,
    BERR, strideBERR,
    WORK,
    IWORK
) → integer
```

| param | type | intent | shape | constraints | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `order` | `Layout` | in |  | one of `'row-major'`, `'column-major'` | storage layout ('row-major' or 'column-major') |
| `fact` | `("not-factored"\|"equilibrate"\|"factored")` | in |  | one of `'equilibrate'`, `'factored'`, `'not-factored'` | specifies whether or not the factored form of the matrix A is supplied on entry, and if not, whether the matrix A should be equilibrated before it is factored. `'factored'`: On entry, AF and IPIV contain the factored form of A. If `equed !== 'none'`, the matrix A has been equilibrated with scaling factors given by R and C. A, AF, and IPIV are not modified. `'not-factored'`: The matrix A will be copied to AF and factored. `'equilibrate'`: The matrix A will be equilibrated if necessary, then copied to AF and factored. |
| `trans` | `TransposeOperation` | in |  | one of `'conjugate-transpose'`, `'no-transpose'`, `'transpose'` | specifies the form of the system of equations: `'no-transpose'`: A * X = B (No transpose) `'transpose'`: A**T * X = B (Transpose) |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  | requires `N ≥ 0` | the number of linear equations, i.e., the order of the matrix A. |
| `nrhs` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  | requires `nrhs ≥ 0` | the number of right hand sides, i.e., the number of columns of the matrices B and X. |
| `A` | `Float64Array` | in/out | `N × N` |  | on entry, the N-by-N matrix A. On exit, if `equed !== 'none'`, A is scaled as follows: `equed === 'row'`: A := diag(R) * A `equed === 'column'`: A := A * diag(C) `equed === 'both'`: A := diag(R) * A * diag(C). |
| ↳ `LDA` | `PositiveInteger` | in |  | requires `LDA ≥ max( 1, N )` | leading dimension of `A` |
| `AF` | `Float64Array` | in/out | `N × N` |  | if `fact === 'factored'`, then AF is an input argument and on entry contains the factors L and U from the factorization A = P*L*U as computed by DGETRF. |
| ↳ `LDAF` | `PositiveInteger` | in |  | requires `LDAF ≥ max( 1, N )` | leading dimension of `AF` |
| `IPIV` | `Int32Array` | in/out | `N` |  | if `fact === 'factored'`, then IPIV is an input argument and on entry contains the pivot indices from the factorization A = P*L*U as computed by DGETRF; row i of the matrix was interchanged with row IPIV(i) (0-based). |
| ↳ `strideIPIV` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride length for `IPIV` |
| `equed` | `Array.<string>` | in/out |  | rejects `fact === 'factored' && !(((equed === 'row' \|\| equed === 'both') \|\| (equed === 'column' \|\| equed === 'both')) \|\| equed === 'none')` | specifies the form of equilibration that was done. `'none'`: No equilibration (always true if `fact === 'not-factored'`). `'row'`: Row equilibration, i.e., A has been premultiplied by diag(R). `'column'`: Column equilibration, i.e., A has been postmultiplied by diag(C). `'both'`: Both row and column equilibration, i.e., A has been replaced by diag(R) * A * diag(C). EQUED is an input argument if `fact === 'factored'`; otherwise, it is an output argument. |

On exit, if `equed === 'none'`, B is not modified; if `trans === 'no-transpose'` and `equed === 'row'` or `equed === 'both'`, B is overwritten by diag(R)*B; if `trans === 'transpose'` and `equed === 'column'` or `equed === 'both'`, B is overwritten by diag(C)*B. |

| `IWORK` | `(Int32Array\|null)` | out | `≥ N` |  | =null] - integer workspace array (length >= N); auto-allocated if null |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `fact`: Specifies whether or not the factored form of the matrix A is supplied on entry, and if not, whether the matrix A should be equilibrated before it is factored.

  -   `= 'F'`: On entry, `AF` and `IPIV` contain the factored form of A. If `EQUED` is not 'N', the matrix A has been equilibrated with scaling factors given by R and C. A, `AF`, and `IPIV` are not modified.
  -   `= 'N'`: The matrix A will be copied to `AF` and factored.
  -   `= 'E'`: The matrix A will be equilibrated if necessary, then copied to `AF` and factored.
- `trans`: Specifies the form of the system of equations:

  -   `= 'N'`: $A \, X = B$     (No transpose)
  -   `= 'T'`: $A^T \, X = B$  (Transpose)
  -   `= 'C'`: $A^H \, X = B$  (Transpose)
- `N`: The number of linear equations, i.e., the order of the matrix A. $N \ge 0$.
- `nrhs`: The number of right hand sides, i.e., the number of columns of the matrices B and X. $\mathrm{NRHS} \ge 0$.
- `A`: On entry, the N-by-N matrix A. If `FACT = 'F'` and `EQUED` is not 'N', then A must have been equilibrated by the scaling factors in R and/or C. A is not modified if `FACT = 'F'` or 'N', or if `FACT = 'E'` and `EQUED = 'N'` on exit.

  On exit, if $\mathrm{EQUED} \ne \text{'N'}$, A is scaled as follows: `EQUED = 'R'`: A := $\operatorname{diag}(R) \, A$ `EQUED = 'C'`: A := $A \, \operatorname{diag}(C)$ `EQUED = 'B'`: A := $\operatorname{diag}(R) \, A \, \operatorname{diag}(C)$.
- `AF`: If `FACT = 'F'`, then `AF` is an input argument and on entry contains the factors L and U from the factorization $A = P \, L \, U$ as computed by DGETRF. If $\mathrm{EQUED} \ne \text{'N'}$, then `AF` is the factored form of the equilibrated matrix A.

  If `FACT = 'N'`, then `AF` is an output argument and on exit returns the factors L and U from the factorization $A = P \, L \, U$ of the original matrix A.

  If `FACT = 'E'`, then `AF` is an output argument and on exit returns the factors L and U from the factorization $A = P \, L \, U$ of the equilibrated matrix A (see the description of A for the form of the equilibrated matrix).
- `IPIV`: If `FACT = 'F'`, then `IPIV` is an input argument and on entry contains the pivot indices from the factorization $A = P \, L \, U$ as computed by DGETRF; row i of the matrix was interchanged with row `IPIV(i)`.

  If `FACT = 'N'`, then `IPIV` is an output argument and on exit contains the pivot indices from the factorization $A = P \, L \, U$ of the original matrix A.

  If `FACT = 'E'`, then `IPIV` is an output argument and on exit contains the pivot indices from the factorization $A = P \, L \, U$ of the equilibrated matrix A.
- `equed`: Specifies the form of equilibration that was done.

  -   `= 'N'`: No equilibration (always true if `FACT = 'N'`).
  -   `= 'R'`: Row equilibration, i.e., A has been premultiplied by diag(R).
  -   `= 'C'`: Column equilibration, i.e., A has been postmultiplied by diag(C).
  -   `= 'B'`: Both row and column equilibration, i.e., A has been replaced by $\operatorname{diag}(R) \, A \, \operatorname{diag}(C)$. `EQUED` is an input argument if `FACT = 'F'`; otherwise, it is an output argument.
- `r`: The row scale factors for A. If `EQUED = 'R'` or 'B', A is multiplied on the left by diag(R); if `EQUED = 'N'` or 'C', R is not accessed. R is an input argument if `FACT = 'F'`; otherwise, R is an output argument. If `FACT = 'F'` and `EQUED = 'R'` or 'B', each element of R must be positive.
- `c`: The column scale factors for A. If `EQUED = 'C'` or 'B', A is multiplied on the right by diag(C); if `EQUED = 'N'` or 'R', C is not accessed. C is an input argument if `FACT = 'F'`; otherwise, C is an output argument. If `FACT = 'F'` and `EQUED = 'C'` or 'B', each element of C must be positive.
- `B`: On entry, the N-by-`NRHS` right hand side matrix B. On exit, if `EQUED = 'N'`, B is not modified; if `TRANS = 'N'` and `EQUED = 'R'` or 'B', B is overwritten by $\operatorname{diag}(R) \, B$; if `TRANS = 'T'` or 'C' and `EQUED = 'C'` or 'B', B is overwritten by $\operatorname{diag}(C) \, B$.
- `X`: If `INFO = 0` or $\mathrm{INFO} = N+1$, the N-by-`NRHS` solution matrix X to the original system of equations. Note that A and B are modified on exit if $\mathrm{EQUED} \ne \text{'N'}$, and the solution to the equilibrated system is $\operatorname{inv}(\operatorname{diag}(C)) \, X$ if `TRANS = 'N'` and `EQUED = 'C'` or 'B', or $\operatorname{inv}(\operatorname{diag}(R)) \, X$ if `TRANS = 'T'` or 'C' and `EQUED = 'R'` or 'B'.
- `rcond`: The estimate of the reciprocal condition number of the matrix A after equilibration (if done). If `RCOND` is less than the machine precision (in particular, if `RCOND = 0`), the matrix is singular to working precision. This condition is indicated by a return code of $\mathrm{INFO} > 0$.
- `FERR`: The estimated forward error bound for each solution vector `X(j)` (the j-th column of the solution matrix X). If XTRUE is the true solution corresponding to `X(j)`, `FERR(j)` is an estimated upper bound for the magnitude of the largest element in (`X(j)` - XTRUE) divided by the magnitude of the largest element in `X(j)`. The estimate is as reliable as the estimate for `RCOND`, and is almost always a slight overestimate of the true error.
- `BERR`: The componentwise relative backward error of each solution vector `X(j)` (i.e., the smallest relative change in any element of A or B that makes `X(j)` an exact solution).
- `WORK`: On exit, `WORK(1)` contains the reciprocal pivot growth factor norm(A)/norm(U). The "max absolute element" norm is used. If `WORK(1)` is much less than 1, then the stability of the LU factorization of the (equilibrated) matrix A could be poor. This also means that the solution X, condition estimator `RCOND`, and forward error bound `FERR` could be unreliable. If factorization fails with $0<\mathrm{INFO} \le N$, then `WORK(1)` contains the reciprocal pivot growth factor for the leading `INFO` columns of A.

</details>

**Returns** `integer`: status code (INFO)

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be a valid order
- `TypeError` second argument must be one of the following: "equilibrate", "factored", "not-factored"
- `TypeError` third argument must be a valid transpose operation
- `RangeError` fourth argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` fifth argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` seventh argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, N )`
- `RangeError` ninth argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, N )`
- `TypeError` twelfth argument is invalid (rejected when `fact === "factored" && !( ( ( equed[ 0 ] === "row" \|\| equed[ 0 ] === "both" ) \|\| ( equed[ 0 ] === "column" \|\| equed[ 0 ] === "both" ) ) \|\| equed[ 0 ] === "none" )`)
- `RangeError` eighteenth argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, N )` (column-major)
- `RangeError` eighteenth argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, nrhs )` (row-major)
- `RangeError` twentieth argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, N )` (column-major)
- `RangeError` twentieth argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, nrhs )` (row-major)
- `TypeError` if a string argument is not a valid option

### Strided (ndarray) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
dgesvx.ndarray(
    fact, trans,
    N, nrhs,
    A, strideA1, strideA2, offsetA,
    AF, strideAF1, strideAF2, offsetAF,
    IPIV, strideIPIV, offsetIPIV,
    equed,
    r, strideR, offsetR,
    c, strideC, offsetC,
    B, strideB1, strideB2, offsetB,
    X, strideX1, strideX2, offsetX,
    rcond,
    FERR, strideFERR, offsetFERR,
    BERR, strideBERR, offsetBERR,
    WORK, strideWork, offsetWork,
    IWORK, strideIwork, offsetIwork
) → integer
```

Expert driver for solving a real system of linear equations A*X = B.
using the LU factorization. Provides equilibration, condition estimation,
iterative refinement, and error bounds.

Matrix shapes are logical (rows × columns). The reference's leading dimension (`LDA`, …) is replaced by the two strides and the offset.

| param | type | intent | shape | constraints | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `fact` | `("not-factored"\|"equilibrate"\|"factored")` | in |  | one of `'equilibrate'`, `'factored'`, `'not-factored'` | `'not-factored'`, `'equilibrate'`, or `'factored'` |
| `trans` | `TransposeOperation` | in |  | one of `'conjugate-transpose'`, `'no-transpose'`, `'transpose'` | `'no-transpose'` or `'transpose'` |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  | requires `N ≥ 0` | order of matrix A |
| `nrhs` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  | requires `nrhs ≥ 0` | number of right-hand side columns |
| `A` | `Float64Array` | in/out | `N × N` |  | N-by-N matrix (may be equilibrated on exit) |
| ↳ `strideA1` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride of the first dimension of A |
| ↳ `strideA2` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride of the second dimension of A |
| ↳ `offsetA` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | index offset for A |
| `AF` | `Float64Array` | in/out | `N × N` |  | N-by-N factored matrix (output) |
| ↳ `strideAF1` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride of the first dimension of AF |
| ↳ `strideAF2` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride of the second dimension of AF |
| ↳ `offsetAF` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | index offset for AF |
| `IPIV` | `Int32Array` | in/out | `N` |  | pivot indices (0-based, output) |
| ↳ `strideIPIV` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride for IPIV |
| ↳ `offsetIPIV` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | index offset for IPIV |
| `equed` | `Array.<string>` | in/out |  | rejects `fact === 'factored' && !(((equed === 'row' \|\| equed === 'both') \|\| (equed === 'column' \|\| equed === 'both')) \|\| equed === 'none')` | equilibration type (input if FACT=`'factored'`) |
| `r` | `Float64Array` | in/out | `N` |  | row scale factors |
| ↳ `strideR` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride for r |
| ↳ `offsetR` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | index offset for r |
| `c` | `Float64Array` | in/out | `N` |  | column scale factors |
| ↳ `strideC` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride for c |
| ↳ `offsetC` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | index offset for c |
| `B` | `Float64Array` | in/out | `N × nrhs` |  | N-by-NRHS right-hand side (may be scaled on exit) |
| ↳ `strideB1` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride of the first dimension of B |
| ↳ `strideB2` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride of the second dimension of B |
| ↳ `offsetB` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | index offset for B |
| `X` | `Float64Array` | out | `N × nrhs` |  | N-by-NRHS solution matrix (output) |
| ↳ `strideX1` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride of the first dimension of X |
| ↳ `strideX2` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride of the second dimension of X |
| ↳ `offsetX` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | index offset for X |
| `rcond` | `Float64Array` | out |  |  | output (length-1 array): the estimate of the reciprocal condition number of the matrix A after equilibration (if done) |
| `FERR` | `Float64Array` | out | `nrhs` |  | forward error bounds (output, length nrhs) |
| ↳ `strideFERR` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride for FERR |
| ↳ `offsetFERR` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | index offset for FERR |
| `BERR` | `Float64Array` | out | `nrhs` |  | backward error bounds (output, length nrhs) |
| ↳ `strideBERR` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride for BERR |
| ↳ `offsetBERR` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | index offset for BERR |
| `WORK` | `Float64Array` | out | `≥ max( 1, 4 * N )` |  | workspace array (length >= max(1, 4*N)) |
| ↳ `strideWork` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride for WORK |

<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `fact`: Specifies whether or not the factored form of the matrix A is supplied on entry, and if not, whether the matrix A should be equilibrated before it is factored.

  -   `= 'F'`: On entry, `AF` and `IPIV` contain the factored form of A. If `EQUED` is not 'N', the matrix A has been equilibrated with scaling factors given by R and C. A, `AF`, and `IPIV` are not modified.

- `N`: The number of linear equations, i.e., the order of the matrix A. $N \ge 0$.
- `nrhs`: The number of right hand sides, i.e., the number of columns of the matrices B and X. $\mathrm{NRHS} \ge 0$.

  If `FACT = 'N'`, then `AF` is an output argument and on exit returns the factors L and U from the factorization $A = P \, L \, U$ of the original matrix A.

  If `FACT = 'E'`, then `AF` is an output argument and on exit returns the factors L and U from the factorization $A = P \, L \, U$ of the equilibrated matrix A (see the description of A for the form of the equilibrated matrix).
- `IPIV`: If `FACT = 'F'`, then `IPIV` is an input argument and on entry contains the pivot indices from the factorization $A = P \, L \, U$ as computed by DGETRF; row i of the matrix was interchanged with row `IPIV(i)`.

  If `FACT = 'N'`, then `IPIV` is an output argument and on exit contains the pivot indices from the factorization $A = P \, L \, U$ of the original matrix A.

  If `FACT = 'E'`, then `IPIV` is an output argument and on exit contains the pivot indices from the factorization $A = P \, L \, U$ of the equilibrated matrix A.
- `equed`: Specifies the form of equilibration that was done.

  -   `= 'N'`: No equilibration (always true if `FACT = 'N'`).
  -   `= 'R'`: Row equilibration, i.e., A has been premultiplied by diag(R).
  -   `= 'C'`: Column equilibration, i.e., A has been postmultiplied by diag(C).
  -   `= 'B'`: Both row and column equilibration, i.e., A has been replaced by $\operatorname{diag}(R) \, A \, \operatorname{diag}(C)$. `EQUED` is an input argument if `FACT = 'F'`; otherwise, it is an output argument.
- `r`: The row scale factors for A. If `EQUED = 'R'` or 'B', A is multiplied on the left by diag(R); if `EQUED = 'N'` or 'C', R is not accessed. R is an input argument if `FACT = 'F'`; otherwise, R is an output argument. If `FACT = 'F'` and `EQUED = 'R'` or 'B', each element of R must be positive.
- `c`: The column scale factors for A. If `EQUED = 'C'` or 'B', A is multiplied on the right by diag(C); if `EQUED = 'N'` or 'R', C is not accessed. C is an input argument if `FACT = 'F'`; otherwise, C is an output argument. If `FACT = 'F'` and `EQUED = 'C'` or 'B', each element of C must be positive.
- `B`: On entry, the N-by-`NRHS` right hand side matrix B. On exit, if `EQUED = 'N'`, B is not modified; if `TRANS = 'N'` and `EQUED = 'R'` or 'B', B is overwritten by $\operatorname{diag}(R) \, B$; if `TRANS = 'T'` or 'C' and `EQUED = 'C'` or 'B', B is overwritten by $\operatorname{diag}(C) \, B$.
- `X`: If `INFO = 0` or $\mathrm{INFO} = N+1$, the N-by-`NRHS` solution matrix X to the original system of equations. Note that A and B are modified on exit if $\mathrm{EQUED} \ne \text{'N'}$, and the solution to the equilibrated system is $\operatorname{inv}(\operatorname{diag}(C)) \, X$ if `TRANS = 'N'` and `EQUED = 'C'` or 'B', or $\operatorname{inv}(\operatorname{diag}(R)) \, X$ if `TRANS = 'T'` or 'C' and `EQUED = 'R'` or 'B'.
- `rcond`: The estimate of the reciprocal condition number of the matrix A after equilibration (if done). If `RCOND` is less than the machine precision (in particular, if `RCOND = 0`), the matrix is singular to working precision. This condition is indicated by a return code of $\mathrm{INFO} > 0$.
- `FERR`: The estimated forward error bound for each solution vector `X(j)` (the j-th column of the solution matrix X). If XTRUE is the true solution corresponding to `X(j)`, `FERR(j)` is an estimated upper bound for the magnitude of the largest element in (`X(j)` - XTRUE) divided by the magnitude of the largest element in `X(j)`. The estimate is as reliable as the estimate for `RCOND`, and is almost always a slight overestimate of the true error.
- `BERR`: The componentwise relative backward error of each solution vector `X(j)` (i.e., the smallest relative change in any element of A or B that makes `X(j)` an exact solution).
- `WORK`: On exit, `WORK(1)` contains the reciprocal pivot growth factor norm(A)/norm(U). The "max absolute element" norm is used. If `WORK(1)` is much less than 1, then the stability of the LU factorization of the (equilibrated) matrix A could be poor. This also means that the solution X, condition estimator `RCOND`, and forward error bound `FERR` could be unreliable. If factorization fails with $0<\mathrm{INFO} \le N$, then `WORK(1)` contains the reciprocal pivot growth factor for the leading `INFO` columns of A.

</details>

**Returns** `integer`: status code (INFO)

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be one of the following: "equilibrate", "factored", "not-factored"
- `TypeError` second argument must be a valid transpose operation
- `RangeError` third argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` fourth argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `TypeError` sixteenth argument is invalid (rejected when `fact === "factored" && !( ( ( equed[ 0 ] === "row" \|\| equed[ 0 ] === "both" ) \|\| ( equed[ 0 ] === "column" \|\| equed[ 0 ] === "both" ) ) \|\| equed[ 0 ] === "none" )`)
- `RangeError` WORK array must have at least max(1,4*N) elements from offset
- `RangeError` IWORK array must have at least N elements from offset

### Status codes

An `info` status code: `0` on success. A positive value reports a numerical condition such as a singular pivot or a failure to converge (see the description). Invalid arguments throw instead of returning a negative `info`.

The reference documents `INFO` as:

-   `= 0`: successful exit
-   `< 0`: if `INFO = -i`, the i-th argument had an illegal value
-   `> 0`: if `INFO = i`, and i is \<= N:  U(i,i) is exactly zero.  The factorization has been completed, but the factor U is exactly singular, so the solution and error bounds could not be computed. `RCOND = 0` is returned. = N+1: U is nonsingular, but `RCOND` is less than machine precision, meaning that the matrix is singular to working precision.  Nevertheless, the solution and error bounds are computed because there are a number of situations where the computed solution can be more accurate than the value of `RCOND` would suggest.

</section>

<!-- /.usage -->

<section class="notes">

## Notes

-   `dgesvx()` corresponds to the reference LAPACK routine [`DGESVX`](https://github.com/Reference-LAPACK/lapack/blob/v3.12.0/SRC/dgesvx.f).

</section>

<!-- /.notes -->

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import Float64Array from '@stdlib/array/float64/lib/index.js';
import Int32Array from '@stdlib/array/int32/lib/index.js';
import dgesvx from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/dgesvx';

const N = 3;
const nrhs = 1;

// Column-major 3x3 matrix and right-hand side (solution is [ 1, 1, 1 ]):
const A = new Float64Array( [ 4.0, 1.0, 0.0, 1.0, 3.0, 1.0, 0.0, 1.0, 2.0 ] );
const AF = new Float64Array( N * N );
const IPIV = new Int32Array( N );
const r = new Float64Array( N );
const c = new Float64Array( N );
const B = new Float64Array( [ 5.0, 5.0, 3.0 ] );
const X = new Float64Array( N * nrhs );
const rcond = new Float64Array( 1 );
const FERR = new Float64Array( nrhs );
const BERR = new Float64Array( nrhs );
const WORK = new Float64Array( 4 * N );
const IWORK = new Int32Array( N );
const equed = [ 'none' ];

// Using the standard interface:
let info = dgesvx( 'column-major', 'not-factored', 'no-transpose', N, nrhs, A, N, AF, N, IPIV, 1, equed, r, 1, c, 1, B, N, X, N, rcond, FERR, 1, BERR, 1, WORK, IWORK );
console.log( info );
// => 0

console.log( X );
// => <Float64Array>[ ~1.0, ~1.0, ~1.0 ]

console.log( equed[ 0 ], rcond[ 0 ], WORK[ 0 ] ); // equilibration, reciprocal condition number, reciprocal pivot growth

// Using the ndarray interface:
equed[ 0 ] = 'none';
info = dgesvx.ndarray( 'not-factored', 'no-transpose', N, nrhs, A, 1, N, 0, AF, 1, N, 0, IPIV, 1, 0, equed, r, 1, 0, c, 1, 0, B, 1, N, 0, X, 1, N, 0, rcond, FERR, 1, 0, BERR, 1, 0, WORK, 1, 0, IWORK, 1, 0 );
console.log( info );
// => 0

console.log( X );
// => <Float64Array>[ ~1.0, ~1.0, ~1.0 ]
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `DGESVX`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

DGESVX uses the LU factorization to compute the solution to a real system of linear equations

$$
A \, X = B
$$

where A is an N-by-N matrix and X and B are N-by-`NRHS` matrices.

Error bounds on the solution and a condition estimate are also provided.

</section>
